title: Adaptive KV-cache allocation with fragmentation-aware slack windows
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: As continuous batching increases throughput, the KV cache allocation pattern becomes more bursty and fragmented across GPU memory. Fragmentation raises p99 latency for long-context requests when the runtime must relocate KV slots or trigger full compaction. Existing slab-like allocations and opportunistic compaction reduce gross memory usage but fail to adapt to dynamic batch-size shifts and multi-tenant pressure.

Goal: Introduce an allocation strategy that maintains fresh allocation slack (short-lived reserved regions) to absorb transient bursts, proactively groups hot KV spans to reduce scatter, and schedules lightweight background reclamation when fragmentation crosses thresholds. This should reduce compaction-triggered stalls, lower tail latency, and improve steady-state token cost by reducing unnecessary evictions and cross-device migrations.
proposed_solution:
1) Segmented slack windows: partition KV pool into stride-aligned segments where each segment maintains a small adaptive slack reservation (a percentage of segment capacity) sized by recent burstiness and batch-size variance.

2) Hot-span affinity map: maintain a compact Bloom-filter backed affinity map mapping model-shard + request-pattern signatures to preferred segments to colocate frequently-reused KV entries. Affinity decays over time.

3) Fragmentation signal and graded compaction: compute a per-GPU fragmentation score (free-run-length distribution + allocation churn) and trigger graded compaction: lightweight local defrag when score > 0.35, aggressive epochal rewrite when > 0.6. Graded compaction runs incrementally to avoid synchronous stalls.

4) Batch-aware eviction thresholds: during large continuous-batching windows temporarily raise eviction reluctance for segments with high hot-span affinity to preserve KV for in-flight sequences; this is timeboxed and bounded by slack usage.

5) Telemetry and feedback loop: expose fragmentation_ratio, slack_utilization, hot_span_hit_rate, compaction_duration to the console and use a controller to anneal slack percentage per segment based on target p99 latency and GPU memory headroom.
acceptance_criteria: p99 generation latency reduced by >= 20% on heavy continuous-batching workloads in lab replay
observed compaction-triggered synchronous stalls per-hour reduced by >= 80% in canary cluster
steady-state KV hit-rate improves or remains +-2% for representative multi-tenant traces
no increase in OOM incidents on dedicated clusters during 48h stress run
new telemetry surfaced in console: fragmentation_ratio, slack_utilization, hot_span_hit_rate
implementation_plan: Spike: implement a userspace simulator using production trace samples to tune segment size and slack annealing (2d)
Design: finalize segment stride, slack sizing heuristics, and compaction thresholds; doc decisions in design doc (3d)
Runtime: implement segment metadata, slack accounting, and hot-span affinity map (7d)
Compaction: add graded compaction worker with rate limits and pause/resume hooks (5d)
Batch integration: wire batch coordinator to signal temporary eviction-reluctance windows (2d)
Telemetry: add metrics and dashboards; hook into rollout controller (2d)
Canary: deploy to dedicated-canary pool and run 72h replay + synthetic stress (3d)
Rollout: progressive ramp across regions with automated rollback on compaction latency anomalies (2d)
testing_plan: Run simulator against three representative traces (chat, long-context summarization, high-throughput streaming) and record fragmentation and token-cost delta
Unit tests for slack accounting, segment boundary correctness, and affinity decay behavior
Integration test: end-to-end generation with synthetic continuous-batching (variable batch sizes up to 16x baseline) verifying p99 and no OOM
Chaos: inject GC/compaction delays to validate that graded compaction avoids system-wide stalls
Performance benchmark: compare throughput and latency against baseline runtime-1.18 on same infra
rollout_plan: Feature gate off by default: enable via runtime flag per-cluster
Canary step 1: 2 dedicated nodes in staging profile for 72h with replay traces
Canary step 2: 10% of dedicated-canary pool with real traffic for 48h
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% of dedicated capacity over 7 days with observability checks at each step
Rollback triggers: compaction_duration p99 increase > 30% or compaction CPU > 40% of host baseline
metrics_and_observability: fragmentation_ratio: percentage computed from free-run-lengths over segment capacity
hot_span_hit_rate: fraction of KV lookups that hit affinity-mapped spans
compaction_events: timestamped events with duration and reclaimed_bytes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Slack over-allocation reduces usable KV capacity and increases evictions. Mitigation: conservative initial slack (2-4%), adaptive annealing downward on low burstiness traces.
Risk: Affinity map false positives cause misplacement and worse locality. Mitigation: use compact filters with per-entry confidence and decay; fall back to LRU placements if affinity hits are low.

Risk: Compaction worker consumes CPU and interferes with inference. Mitigation: rate limit background compaction and schedule during low-util windows; expose controller to temporarily disable on high CPU.
Risk: Unanticipated multi-tenant interactions. Mitigation: start on dedicated clusters first and expand after tenant-specific telemetry validates behavior.
